The planner falsified its own predecessor's named next target (the annulus-slack lower bound is false at `f = g`) and instead specified the finite zero-divisor extraction that sprint 005's machinery had been assuming without any theorem producing it. The generator returned `STATUS=READY_FOR_EVALUATION`, shipping `Proof/BlaschkeNormalForm.lean` (663 lines, axiom-free) plus a re-routed `Candidates/V6.lean`, and the evaluator returned `STATUS=VERDICT_PASS` with score **17823/50000** — deliberately equal to parent V5, which the evaluator independently re-measured rather than taking on trust, since this sprint ships a layer rather than a number. Verdict note: `ProofRefinement/Korenblum/Refinement_Log/verdict_sprint_006_blaschke_normal_form.md`. The generator returned `STATUS=READY_FOR_EVALUATION`, having shipped `Proof/MultiplierForm.lean` (~370 lines, axiom-free) with the full round trip `ValidKorenblumBound c ↔ 0 < c ∧ c < 1 ∧ MultiplierBound c`, the analytic-quotient existence lemma closed on its first route, and — the calibration payoff — `korenblum_ceiling : ValidKorenblumBound c → c² ≤ 1/2`, the project's first hard upper bound, putting the shipped `c_value = 0.35646` at 50.4 % of `1/√2`. The evaluator returned `STATUS=VERDICT_PASS`: build clean, no `sorry` (the single grep hit at `Proof/MultiplierForm.lean:34` is docstring prose), axiom audit exactly the four seeds, no oracles, and **score 17823/50000** — equal to parent V6, which is what this contract specifies, since it ships a layer and a ceiling rather than a number. Verdict note: `ProofRefinement/Korenblum/Refinement_Log/verdict_sprint_007_multiplier_normal_form.md`. Bulletin event line appended; next target per the planner is the weight reduction via the log-subharmonic Poisson bound on `|G|²`, whose two endpoint cases are both already provable.
